methodologyNotes: Covers street-legal, currently-sold two-wheeled motorcycles offered at a published US MSRP. Excludes scooters, mopeds, off-road-only / closed-course competition bikes, three-wheelers, and side-by-sides. Price is base US MSRP in USD, excluding destination and setup. motorcycleType is the manufacturer/segment class as an enum (cruiser, touring, sport, sport-touring, adventure, naked, standard, dual-sport). engineDisplacementCc is total engine displacement in cubic centimeters (cc). engineConfiguration is an enum describing cylinder layout (single, parallel-twin, v-twin, inline-3, inline-4, v4, boxer-twin). horsepowerHp is manufacturer-claimed peak crankshaft power in horsepower (hp); null if not disclosed. torqueLbFt is manufacturer-claimed peak torque in pound-feet (lb-ft); null if not disclosed. seatHeightIn is standard/unladen seat height in inches. wetWeightLbs is curb / wet weight (all fluids and full fuel tank) in pounds; if the maker lists only dry weight, that is noted in provenance. fuelCapacityGal is fuel tank capacity in US gallons. transmissionSpeeds is the number of forward gears as an integer. finalDrive is an enum (chain, belt, shaft). coolingType is an enum (liquid, air, oil-air). absEquipped is a boolean: true if anti-lock braking is standard equipment.

products.name: Harley-Davidson Street Glide
products.priceNote: Base US MSRP. Harley-Davidson official product page states "Starting at $24,999"; Autotrader lists "Start Price $24,999" and "MSRP 24999" for the 2026 Harley-Davidson Touring Street Glide. Per methodology this base MSRP excludes destination and setup.
products.provenance: The official Harley-Davidson product page confirms this exact model (2026 Street Glide, base FLHX, "Starting at $24,999") and verbatim lists a "liquid-cooled Milwaukee-Eight 117 motor", Horsepower "105 HP", Engine Torque "130 ft-lbs", "Weight, In Running Order 811 lb" (curb/wet), "Fuel Capacity 6 gal.", and gear ratios 1st through 6th (six-speed); it gives seat height only as "Seat Height, Laden 26.4 in." (not the unladen figure the methodology requires, so seatHeightIn is null), states displacement only as "117 cu in." (no cc, so null), and lists only "Primary Drive: Chain" with no belt final drive stated (finalDrive null). Autotrader's 2026 Harley-Davidson Touring Street Glide page corroborates the base model at "Start Price $24,999" / "MSRP 24999", "Horsepower (bhp) 105", "Fuel Capacity (gal) 6", "Engine Type V Twin" (mapped to v-twin), and "Generic Type (Primary) Touring". Autotrader lists 774 lb as dry weight, so the manufacturer's 811 lb "In Running Order" figure is used for wet weight; ABS is described as standard rider-safety equipment on the H-D page.

products.name: BMW R 1300 GS

The product page (corroboration) lists the base US MSRP verbatim as "$20,395" (excludes $1,095 destination/handling). coolingType is left null because BMW states "Air/liquid-cooled", a hybrid that does not map cleanly to the liquid/air/oil-air enum.

That same page supplied every non-null spec verbatim: "1084cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin four-stroke", "Six-speed manual" transmission, "#525 Chain" final drive, seat height "34.3 inches (standard position)", "Curb Weight 510 pounds (includes... a full tank of fuel)", "Fuel Capacity 5.0 gallons", and ABS on both front and rear brakes. products.name: Yamaha MT-09

This is the base standard MT-09, distinct from the MT-09 SP ($12,699) and the Y-AMT variant. products.provenance: The Yamaha Motorsports USA specs page for the 2025 MT-09 confirmed model identity — the base "MT-09", explicitly distinct from the "MT-09 SP" ($12,699) in the same lineup — and rendered the full US spec sheet verbatim: "890cc liquid-cooled, DOHC, inline 3-cylinder", 6-speed transmission, "Final Drive Chain", "Fuel Capacity 3.7 gal", "Seat Height 32.5 in", "Wet Weight 425 lb", dual 298mm front / 245mm rear hydraulic discs with ABS, plus base MSRP "$10,899". products.name: Kawasaki Ninja 500
products.priceNote: Base US MSRP $5,299 for the 2024 Kawasaki Ninja 500 (non-ABS). Cycle World states "Ninja 500 non-ABS ($5,299)" and lists "MSRP: $5,299 / $5,699–$5,899 (ABS)"; Motorcycle.com lists "2024 Kawasaki Ninja 500 Base $5,299 MSRP" (ABS variant $5,699). Excludes destination charge ($450 per Motorcycle.com).
products.provenance: The official Kawasaki product page was unreachable (network-blocked) and RevZilla returned 403, so this entry is sourced from two fetched pages for this exact model. Cycle World's dated Aug 6 2024 buyer's guide confirms the 2024 Kawasaki Ninja 500 as a 451cc DOHC liquid-cooled parallel-twin sportbike (successor to the Ninja 400) with a claimed 51 hp, 31.7 lb-ft, 30.9 in seat height, 370 lb wet weight (non-ABS), 3.7 gal tank, 6-speed/chain drive, and base MSRP $5,299 non-ABS. Motorcycle.com's spec sheet independently corroborates the model identity and figures — Type "Sport", Engine Type "Parallel Twin", 451cc, 51 hp, Liquid cooling, 6 speeds, chain drive, 3.7 gal, and the "2024 Kawasaki Ninja 500 Base $5,299 MSRP"; absEquipped is set false because the base Ninja 500 is the non-ABS variant (ABS is a separately priced model, not standard equipment).

products.name: Ducati Monster
products.priceNote: Base US MSRP $12,995 for the base Monster (Dark Stealth) per the official Ducati US page ("Monster - Dark Stealth $12,995*"; "Starting from $12,995"). Excludes the $995 destination charge, taxes, and setup per methodology (base MSRP, destination/setup excluded).
products.provenance: The official Ducati US page (requested URL redirected to /monster-937, titled "Ducati Monster 937 in the USA | Naked Sport Motorcycle") provided the full tech spec for the base Monster and its base MSRP of $12,995 (Dark Stealth, "Starting from $12,995"), which excludes the $995 destination charge — confirming model identity as the standard 937 Monster, not the SP/+/30° Anniversario/Senna variants. It lists a 937 cc Testastretta 11° V2-90° liquid-cooled engine, 111 hp @ 9,250 rpm, 69 lb ft torque, 6-speed gearbox with chain final drive, standard Cornering ABS, 32.3 in standard seat, and a 3.7 US gal tank; Ducati states weight only as "wet weight no fuel" 395 lb (179 kg). The Motorcycle.com 2022 Monster 937 spec page corroborates identical engine/chassis figures (111 hp, 69 lb-ft, 937 cc, liquid cooling, 6 speeds, chain, ABS Standard, 32.3 in, 3.7 gal) and lists the full curb "Wet Weight 414 lb (188 kg)" — the value used here per the methodology's all-fluids/full-fuel-tank definition — plus an Introduction Year of 2021.

products.name: Indian Scout
products.priceNote: Base US MSRP $13,999 for the 2025 Scout Classic (Standard trim), excluding destination/setup. Cycle News: "Scout Classic: Starting at $13,999". Total Motorcycle: "US MSRP Price: $13,999 to $15,199 USD" (top of range is the Limited +Tech trim).
products.provenance: "Indian Scout" maps to the 2025 Indian Scout Classic (Standard trim) — the heritage/base model of Indian's current Scout family. The 2025 redesign replaced the single former "Scout" with five models (Scout Classic, Scout Bobber, Sport Scout, Super Scout, 101 Scout); there is no plain "Scout" trim, and the Classic is the direct heir carrying traditional Scout styling. Indian's official site returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching, so Cycle News (dated April 3, 2024), which reproduces Indian's official press-release spec table, is the verifiable primary source, corroborated by Total Motorcycle's reproduction of Indian's full official spec sheet. Both confirm the Scout Classic's $13,999 base US MSRP (Standard trim), the SpeedPlus 1250cc liquid-cooled 60-degree V-twin, 105 hp / 82 lb-ft claimed (the 111 hp figure applies only to the 101 Scout), 6-speed transmission, belt final drive, 3.4 gal fuel, and standard ABS across the lineup. wetWeightLbs = 555 lb is the "Running Order / Full of Fuel" weight (the empty-tank figure is 536 lb) per the methodology's full-fuel convention; seatHeightIn = 26.8 in is the unladen figure ("Seat Height (Unladen) 26.8 in" / 680 mm; the 25.7 in figure is laden) per the methodology's unladen convention.
